title: Blaze: An Efficient Bit-Sparse Attention Architecture With Workload Orchestration Optimization
problem: Attention mechanisms have high computational complexity and power consumption in NLP models; existing bit-sparsity methods focus on CNNs and don't address workload imbalance and hardware under-utilization caused by irregular distribution of non-zero bits in attention tensors.
motivation: Attention is the core primitive in modern NLP, but its quadratic complexity and high memory bandwidth demands make it a critical bottleneck for efficient inference.
method: Blaze speeds up attention mechanisms in AI models by exploiting sparsity at two levels: skipping zero values and skipping zero bits within individual numbers. However, these non-zero bits don't spread evenly across the data—some hardware ends up idle while other parts get overloaded. Blaze solves this load imbalance with an Approximate-Computing-Based (ACB) workload orchestration system, which redistributes computations and allows small approximation errors when necessary to keep hardware running at full capacity. It also includes a Leading-Booth mechanism that optimizes bit-serial computation (processing data one bit at a time) and runs all of this on a reconfigurable computing engine that can adapt between different computation strategies.
key_novelty: Blaze's core innovation is combining an Approximate-Computing-Based workload orchestration mechanism with a Leading-Booth enhancement for bit-serial processing to solve the load imbalance problem in sparse attention hardware.
contributions: Bit-level and value-level sparsity exploitation tailored for attention mechanisms
Approximate-Computing-Based (ACB) workload orchestration to mitigate load imbalance from irregular bit patterns
Leading-Booth mechanism to enhance bit-serial attention computation performance
Reconfigurable computing engine supporting both ACB and Leading-Booth mechanisms
2.37-6.18x performance improvement and 9.69-43.96x energy efficiency vs SOTA attention accelerators; 1.58x vs SOTA bit-sparse accelerators

metrics.speedup: 2.37-6.18x vs SOTA attention accelerators; 1.58x vs SOTA bit-sparse accelerators

limitations: Abstract does not discuss memory bandwidth requirements, comparison with other sparsity-aware attention approaches, or applicability to other transformer components (e.g., feedforward).
